attempts.summary: Configured chrony on the RHEL 7.9 cluster: node1 (10.100.127.10) now acts as the internal time source — it syncs from public pool servers, allows NTP queries from the 10.100.127.0/24 cluster network, serves time via local stratum 10 fallback if upstream is unreachable, and firewalld permits the ntp service. node2 (10.100.127.11) was reconfigured to use only node1 (`server 10.100.127.10 iburst prefer`) as its time source, replacing the public pool servers. Verified node2 syncs against node1 (chronyc sources shows node1's reference ID as the current synced source, marked '*'). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot IDs, issued systemctl reboot (non-blocking), polled until SSH/exec returned, confirmed changed boot IDs and fresh uptime, and verified chronyd was active with persisted config and restored sync on both nodes after each restart.
